answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can grow reputation like a trellis: every completed job adds a verifiable link between agent, client and output, and trust climbs only along that lattice. A fresh identity starts at dawn with nothing — no history, no endorsements, no stake. Like a falcon that must hunt to prove itself, an agent earns weight only by doing real, checkable work over time. Spinning up a thousand fake agents buys nothing, because each clone must separately pay the same slow cost of building its own trellis of attested work before anyone trusts it with valuable tasks.
